featuredReason: 本文虽以大田喷洒无人机为主，但其中关于无人机在恶劣天气下替代地面机械作业、多光谱遥感集成、混合动力趋势以及FAA执照审批流程等内容，对智慧畜牧从业者理解农业无人机在牧场管理、饲料地植保和遥感监测中的应用前景具有直接参考价值。

Drones now delivering more options on the farm

Drones are doing more now on the farm than ever before. Jeff Clack of Bestway Ag will be on hand at the Sunbelt Ag Expo to demonstrate some of these new capabilities.

Brad Haire,Executive Editor,Farm PressOctober 7, 2026

schedule4 Min Read

Jeff Clack is chief supervisor of operations for Bestway Ag Drones. He, his team and their ag drones will be part of the field demonstrations at the Darrell Williams Research Farm during the Sunbelt Ag Expo.Shelley E. Huguley

At a Glance

In addition to spraying, ag drones can also capture imagery from above.

Drones have an advantage over traditional farm equipment when the weather is bad and vehicles can’t get into fields.

Getting proper licensing for an ag drone can be a lengthy, but necessary, process.

Spray drones have flown beyond being a niche or novel part of modern agriculture to become a valuable tool on many operations. But questions remain: What can they do now for farmers, and what will their capabilities be in the future?

Jeff Clack is chief supervisor of operations for Bestway Ag Drones and a certified drone operator. He, his team and their drones will be part of the field demonstrations at the Darrell Williams Research Farm during the three-day Sunbelt Ag Expo starting Oct. 20.

“We can do more than just spray with drones,” Clack said. “We can do imagery with a multispectral drone that’s very affordable. Integrating a drone into the airspace puts a unique tool in our toolbox.”

Clack and Bestway Ag will be located just behind the Sunbelt Ag Expo farm shop, near where visitors load the trams to tour the farm’s demonstration plots.

“Many in agriculture are familiar with drones,” Clack said. “During the Expo, or any time, we want to engage with individuals to answer their questions or clear up any myths or concerns about spray drones. We want growers to come see us so we can answer any specific questions they have for drones in their operations and personalize the conversation to what they need.”

Related:Camso tracks get new Michelin name but use same soil-saving technology

The team will have several models of DJI spray drones, including the Agras and Mavic lines, along with accompanying trailers.

“We will map out the field with a Mavic 3 Multispectral drone,” Clack explained. “We will load that information to a spray drone and show in our demonstrations what drone capabilities are, as far as being able to spray and be integrated into a farming operation.”

For example, one of the drones will be the Agras T50. A coaxial twin-rotor powers the drone, and it can carry up to 10 gallons of liquid or about 110 pounds of dry material. The battery is good for about nine minutes of flight time, which can spray 5 to 6 acres per charge.

Clack added that drones prove their worth when fields are muddy and ground rigs cannot apply products in a timely manner, which was the case for many parts of the Southeast this growing season.

“If a fungicide must be applied as soon as possible, and rain comes several days prior to spray time, it will be a while before you can get a ground rig in to take care of that field. Drones don’t have that problem,” he said.

Obstacles

Battery life is a challenge for spray drone technology right now, Clack said.

“I see drones, as a whole, getting larger and larger,” he said. “But now what that means is we have to incorporate better power systems. And what I’m seeing is a trend to hybridized power systems,” a system that incorporates fuel-based power in conjunction with battery power.

Related:New 5E tractor with electronic transmission ideal for small farms

“Operators often run two generators to keep their flight batteries charged all the time, plus run mix and fill systems for a full day of spraying,” Clack added. “Keeping those generators running constantly creates its own challenges. So the trend is to get those onboard power generation systems on the drone to let them generate their own power.”

Training

Clack said it takes time and planning to get the training and necessary licenses to use the heavy drones legally. The required FAA third-class medical certificate, administered by an aviation medical provider, also takes time.

“The license is necessary, and it requires some study,” Clack said. “It’s a 60-question test requiring 70% to pass. Is it passable without studying? Not usually. So you have to put a little study time in. Several online courses are available.”

Licenses cost $175. Cost for smaller drones (less than 55 pounds) can be registered online through FAA for $5.

“Registering drones over 55 pounds is a wet-ink process and must be mailed in with a public notary endorsement,” Clack said. “The process can take as much as 90 days. They will look at everything and get a tail number. The drone must be registered. As soon as your drone registration number comes back in a certificate, the aircraft is legal to fly.”

Related:Father and son restore revolutionary Ford 971 tractor

Clack is based out of Crestview, Fla., and has more than 30 years of experience in the ag equipment industry, spending his last four years with Bestway Ag, which is based in Hopkinsville, Ky.

Shelley E. Huguley, Farm Press senior editor, contributed to this article.

translationZh:
无人机如今在农场中发挥的作用比以往任何时候都大。Bestway Ag的Jeff Clack将在Sunbelt Ag Expo上现场演示其中一些新功能。

Jeff Clack是Bestway Ag Drones的首席运营主管。他、他的团队及其农业无人机将参加Sunbelt Ag Expo期间在Darrell Williams研究农场进行的田间演示。

**概览**

除了喷洒作业外，农业无人机还可以从空中采集影像。

在天气恶劣、传统农机无法进入田地时，无人机具有明显优势。

为农业无人机取得适当执照可能是一个漫长的过程，但这是必要的。

喷洒无人机已经超越了作为现代农业小众或新奇工具的阶段，成为许多农场运营中的宝贵工具。但问题仍然存在：它们现在能为农民做什么，未来的能力又将如何？

Jeff Clack是Bestway Ag Drones的首席运营主管，也是一名持证无人机操作员。他、他的团队及其无人机将参加从10月20日开始的为期三天的Sunbelt Ag Expo期间在Darrell Williams研究农场进行的田间演示。

Clack说：“我们用无人机能做的不仅仅是喷洒。我们可以用一架非常实惠的多光谱无人机进行影像采集。将无人机融入空域，为我们的工具箱增添了一件独特的工具。”

Clack和Bestway Ag的位置就在Sunbelt Ag Expo农场车间后面，靠近游客乘坐游览车参观农场示范田的乘车点。

Clack说：“农业领域的许多人都熟悉无人机。在博览会期间，或者任何时候，我们都希望与个人交流，回答他们的问题，或澄清关于喷洒无人机的任何误解或疑虑。我们希望种植者来看我们，这样我们就能回答他们对无人机在其运营中的任何具体问题，并根据他们的需求个性化对话。”

**相关阅读：** Camso履带更名米其林品牌，但仍采用相同的护土技术

该团队将展示多款DJI喷洒无人机，包括Agras和Mavic系列，以及配套拖车。

Clack解释说：“我们将用一架Mavic 3多光谱无人机对田地进行测绘。我们将把这些信息加载到喷洒无人机上，并在演示中展示无人机的能力，包括喷洒以及融入农场运营的能力。”

例如，其中一架无人机将是Agras T50。该无人机采用同轴双旋翼动力系统，最多可携带10加仑液体或约110磅干物料。电池可支持约9分钟飞行时间，每次充电可喷洒5至6英亩。

Clack补充说，当田地泥泞、地面机械无法及时施用产品时，无人机就证明了其价值，本生长季东南部许多地区就是这种情况。

他说：“如果必须尽快施用杀菌剂，而喷洒前又下了几天雨，那么要等很长时间才能让地面机械进入田间处理。无人机没有这个问题。”

**障碍**

Clack说，电池续航是目前喷洒无人机技术面临的一个挑战。

他说：“我认为无人机整体上会越来越大。但现在这意味着我们必须整合更好的动力系统。我看到的一个趋势是混合动力系统，”即结合燃油动力和电池动力的系统。

Clack补充说：“操作员通常运行两台发电机来保持飞行电池始终充电，同时运行混合和加注系统以支持一整天的喷洒。让这些发电机持续运转本身就带来了挑战。因此，趋势是让无人机搭载机载发电系统，使其能够自行发电。”

**培训**

Clack说，要合法使用重型无人机，获得培训和必要执照需要时间和规划。所需的FAA三级体检证明由航空体检机构颁发，也需要时间。

Clack说：“执照是必要的，而且需要一些学习。这是一项60道题的考试，需要70%才能通过。不学习能通过吗？通常不能。所以你必须投入一些学习时间。有几门在线课程可供选择。”

执照费用为175美元。较小无人机（低于55磅）可以通过FAA网站在线注册，费用为5美元。

Clack说：“注册超过55磅的无人机是一个湿墨签字流程，必须邮寄并附公证人背书。这个过程可能需要长达90天。他们会审查所有内容并分配一个尾号。无人机必须注册。一旦你的无人机注册号以证书形式返回，该飞行器就可以合法飞行了。”

**相关阅读：** 父子修复革命性的福特971拖拉机

Clack常驻佛罗里达州Crestview，在农业设备行业拥有30多年经验，最近四年在总部位于肯塔基州Hopkinsville的Bestway Ag工作。

Farm Press高级编辑Shelley E. Huguley对本文有贡献。
